productSummary:
Remi is a personal workflow dashboard for one investment analyst at Ninety One who is moving from Private Credit (PC) to Fixed Income (FI). The move date is a placeholder, Mon 4 Jan 2027, stored as MOVE. Everything runs only on the user's Mac, and the prototype's 'today' is pinned to Mon 5 Oct 2026, BD3.

What Remi plans, at business-day (BD) level, about 3 months ahead:
- BAU (recurring work). PC BAU follows business-day rules, e.g. BD3 fund and security-level returns for 12 funds (6h), and BD8 ManCo pack (4h). FI BAU is a eurozone sovereign country rotation that starts on the move date.
- Goal-first projects. Each has a charter, a rolling-wave plan (Now milestones with estimated tasks, Next milestones, and one line of Later intent), check-ins, a scope log, snapshots, a premortem risk list and, for PC, an exit route.

How it works:
- A pure engine derives per-day load and capacity (8h/day), forecasts, flags (at risk, overload, stale) and a move verdict. The verdict answers 'Am I on track to move cleanly?' and depends on every PC exit landing before MOVE, and on the returns pipeline landing before the December BD3 run (DEC_RUN, Thu 3 Dec 2026) that the successor must shadow.
- The main source of change is scope growth, fed in through check-ins. A free-text 'Tell Remi' update is parsed by an LLM, or by a regex fallback, into typed change proposals. The user reviews them before anything is applied.
- The signature UX is 'the plan moves'. Bars glide on a spring, a ghost of the previous plan appears, dates roll like an odometer, and a +N BD chip shows.

Surfaces:
1. A Home launcher.
2. The 'Control Panel' app: an 88px nav rail, a 72px header, eight always-mounted screens (Today, Notes, Timeline, Calendar, Projects, Project workspace, Routines, Transition), a right-hand check-in drawer (1160px) and a ⌘K command palette.
3. A standalone Notion-style Textbook for numbered study notes, with KaTeX formulas and sandboxed live HTML charts. It is not in SPEC.md.
4. A Foundations design-system page.

Current state: the prototype is Claude Design .dc.html files running on a generated runtime (support.js), with all state held in localStorage ('remi.v1' and 'remi.textbook.v1').

Production target:
- A React + TypeScript SPA (Vite) using design tokens as CSS variables.
- A pure TypeScript engine package shared by the UI and the API. The client needs synchronous calendar and forecast maths for layout and live previews.
- A local-only API bound to 127.0.0.1. SPEC recommends Node + Hono + SQLite via Drizzle. It uses the user's folder architecture: core, schemas, repositories, services, utils, api.
- Persistence in SQLite, with an append-only event log as the source of truth (SPEC §7).
- AI calls proxied server-side, subject to compliance.

Colours and fonts are brand stand-ins until the Ninety One template arrives. Components must read tokens only, so the brand swap touches :root and nothing else.

screens.name: Home (launcher)
screens.summary:
Standalone page with no nav rail. The prototype renders it on a fixed 1920x1080 stage scaled with min(vw/1920, vh/1080) and letterboxed in color-mix(ink 6%, paper).

Layout:
- Header bar: 88px tall, 120px side insets, hairline bottom border. Left: serif 'Remi' wordmark at 26px. Right: 'Mon 5 Oct · BD3', a divider, then '61 business days to Fixed Income'. All of this text is hard-coded.
- Hero: at left 120, top 176, width 1100. Greeting in small caps 'Good morning|afternoon|evening · Monday 5 October' (the time-of-day word comes from the real clock). H1 in Libre Caslon 92px/1.02, letter-spacing -0.025em: 'Where to this morning|afternoon|evening?'.
- Two 816x560 cards in a 2-column grid at top 388 with a 48px gap. Cards have paper-raised background, 6px radius, an inset hairline border, and padding 34 40 30.

Card 01 'Control Panel':
- Description: 'Today, the timeline, projects, routines and the move, recalculated as you go.'
- Decorative animated preview: a 30-bar capacity strip (CAP array; CAPH on hover), 5 mini Gantt rows, a today line at 4% and a move line at 84%.
- Footer: 'Returns pipeline', a Roll 'Wed 2 Dec', and a '+3 BD' pill. On hover these become 'Fri 4 Dec' and '+5 BD'. Also a meta line '{n} projects · {n} routines · {n} notes today'.

Card 02 'Textbook':
- Description: 'Numbered notes, clean formulas and live charts you drop in from Claude.'
- Typeset primer excerpt with the formula ΔP / P ≈ −D × Δy.
- On hover: 'Convexity' types out (steps(9), 520ms) and a slash menu appears after 560ms.
- Footer: '{N} pages · {M} live chart(s)'.

Card hover: border turns ink, the card lifts -4px, and the round arrow button fills ink.

Clicking a card, or pressing 1 or 2, plays the expand overlay: the card rect becomes the full stage over 420ms spring, then navigation happens at +520ms.

Page footer: 'Press [1] or [2] to jump straight in' and 'A personal instrument. Nothing here is shared.'

Data: counts are read from localStorage today. Production reads them from GET /api/home/summary.

Note: the screenshots show an older copy ('IN THE WORKS' badge, a sub-headline). The code is the source of truth.
keyComponents: ControlPanelCard preview (capacity strip, mini Gantt, Roll forecast + delta pill)

Grid: 88px nav rail | minmax(0,1fr). The right column has grid-template-rows 72px header | main.

Nav rail (border-right hairline, padding 22px 0 20px, gap 4px), top to bottom:
- Home button: 'Remi' in serif 22px over '‹ Home' at 10px. It fades the app to opacity 0 over 180ms, then routes to Home.
- 7 nav buttons, each 72x62, with a Material Symbol at 22px wght 300 and an 11px/500 label: Today [today], Notes [notes], Timeline [view_timeline], Calendar [calendar_month], Projects [stacks, also active on the workspace], Routines [repeat], Transition [arrow_forward].
  - Active: paper-raised background, hairline border, ink text.

Header (padding 0 48px, gap 28px, hairline bottom border), left to right:
- Date 'Mon 5 Oct' (17/600) · 'BD3' (mono 13).
- 1x22 divider.

- Spacer.

screens.name: Today
screens.summary:
Default screen. Padding 40 48 48. Grid 7fr/5fr with column-gap 72. At 1920 the left column is about 971px and the right about 693px.

LEFT column. The day-switch animation applies only here. It has three blocks with arrival delays 0, 40 and 80ms.

(1) Day header
- Kicker: 'Today' | 'Tomorrow · preview' | '<Weekday> · N business days ahead'. Plus a 'Back to today' pill when previewing.
- H1: serif 52px/1.1, the long date, e.g. 'Monday 5 October'.
- Meta line: 'BD3 of 22' (mono) · '8h working day' · verdict.word in ink.

(2) Capacity
- Title 'Today’s capacity' / '<Weekday>’s capacity'. Label '8h of 8h planned · 0h free', or '9.5h planned · 1.5h over' in overload colour.
- A 14px segmented bar. BAU segments are split into ceil(h) hour cells in the accent colour. Project segments use the soft fill with an accent outline. Free space is an outline. There is an 8h capacity marker, and the bar pulses when over.
- Legend: BAU / Project / Free.

(3) Plan
- Title 'Today’s plan', with the note 'BAU first, then focus blocks' (preview: 'As planned today; it moves if the plan does').
- Rows use a 64px hours gutter at 24/500.
- Returns BAU card, shown only when r-ret runs that day:
  - 'BAU · Private Credit', 'BD3, monthly', 'Routine ↗'.
  - Title 'Fund & security-level returns', a Roll count, and 'of 12 funds'.
  - A 2px progress line, then a 3-column checklist of the 12 funds.
  - Interactive on today only. Preview shows it unchecked with 'Fresh checklist for this run · ticking opens on the day'.
- Other BAU rows, e.g. 'BD8 · automating', or the rotation row '4h a day'.
- NoBau row: 'No BAU on this day. The next run is <date>.'
- Project focus blocks, one per project with hours that day:
  - 'Project · <domain>', 'Focus block', the name, 'Workspace ↗'.
  - The goal in serif italic 17px.
  - The Now tasks sliced to fit that day's hours, with 18px checkboxes.
  - Milestone line: '◆ Next milestone: <name> · <date>'.

RIGHT column (arrival delays 120 and 160ms).

(4) Week strip
- Title 'This week' / 'Week of D Mon'. Subtitle '5–9 Oct · pick a day to preview it'.
- Five day cards (Mon–Fri of the selected day's week), each with:
  - a label and BD number;
  - a 6px mini capacity bar;
  - '7h of 8h' or '9.5h · over';
  - BAU chips 'Returns 6h' and milestone chips '◆ name';
  - up to 2 project items with a bar (h/4 width) and hours;
  - '+N more'.
- Selected card: 2px ink top border and paper-raised background.

(5) Month snapshot
- Always today's month. Title 'October so far', with a Roll 'N of M done · K overdue'.
- Cumulative bar chart, one bar per BD, 60px tall: outline = due by then, late fill = risk 55% mixed with paper, done fill = ink.
- Axis '1 Oct' to '30 Oct'. Legend Done / Overdue / Due by then.
- Two groups, BAU (limit 4) and Projects (limit 5), each with a mini progress bar and count. Rows are 16px checkboxes with due labels: 'done 5 Oct' / 'overdue 1 BD' / 'today' / 'Thu 15 Oct'. 'Show N more and M done' / 'Show less'.

Hover on any item sets the global hover id. Other items dim to 0.3 (bar segments to 0.25).

Computed but NOT rendered: the 'What changed' feed, 'Needs attention' and the check-in prompt card. SPEC and the older screenshots have them; restoring them is an open question.

screens.name: Notes
screens.summary:
Three-column grid: 300px | minmax(0,1fr) | 340px.

LEFT 'Notebook' rail:
- Header: kicker 'Notebook' and '6 notes across 3 days'.
- Scroll list of days, descending:
  - every business day from today back 27 calendar days;
  - plus any day in that window that has notes;
  - plus older days that have notes.
- Week headers: 'This week' / 'Week of 28 Sep'.
- Day rows: 'Today · Mon 5 Oct' or 'Fri 2 Oct', a count, and a one-line serif preview of the latest note. Empty days show 'No notes' / 'Nothing yet today' in italic.
- Selected row: paper-raised background with an inset hairline.

CENTRE (max 820px, centred, padding 36 56 80):
- Kicker: 'Today' / 'Last business day' / 'N business days ago' / holiday name / 'Weekend', plus a '‹ Today' pill.
- H1: serif 48px.
- Sub line: 'BD3 · 3 notes · <top 3 mentions>'.
- Composer:
  - 64px time column: live HH:MM on today, '—:—' otherwise.
  - Serif 20px auto-grow textarea. Placeholder 'Jot something down…' or 'Add a note to Fri 2 Oct…'.
  - Live tag chips.
  - Hint 'Enter to jot · Shift+Enter for a new line'.
  - Enter adds the note.
- Entries, newest first:
  - Mono time and an inline-editable serif 18px textarea.
  - Blur commits. A blank value deletes the note. Escape reverts.
  - Clickable tag chips open the project workspace or routine.
  - A just-added note is tinted pc-accent 7% for 1400ms, then fades over 900ms.
- Empty-state copy for today and for other days.

RIGHT rail (paper-raised, padding 32):
- 'Remi reads these' with an explanation.
- CTA 'Turn this day into an update'. It opens Tell Remi prefilled with the day's notes as 'HH:MM text' lines. When the day is empty it reads 'Nothing to send yet' and is disabled.
- Note: 'Remi currently has N recent notes as background' (last 5 BDs).
- 'Mentioned on this day': tag, name, count.
- 'This week': Mon–Fri spark bars. Bar height = count/max(3, max) with a 440ms spring. Clicking a bar selects that day.

Day switch: fade and translateY ±6px. The swap happens at 120ms, then the composer is focused. The composer is autofocused 320ms after arriving on the screen.

screens.name: Calendar
screens.summary:
Month grid. Padding 28 48 32, min-height 880.

Header:
- Kicker 'Calendar'. Title in serif 28px, e.g. 'October 2026'.
- Mono sub-line: '22 business days' or '21 business days · 1 overloaded'.
- Legend: BAU chip, project hours, milestone.
- Nav: prev, 'This month', next. Prev/next dim to 0.35 at the ends of the range.

Grid:
- Columns repeat(5, minmax(0,1fr)) 64px 64px, i.e. wide Mon–Fri and narrow Sat/Sun.
- Weekday heads have a 1px ink bottom rule.
- Rows share the available height (5 or 6 rows).

- Selected cell: 1.5px inset ink ring.

- Kicker: 'Today' / 'Tomorrow' / 'N business days ahead' / 'N business days ago' / 'Weekend' / 'Bank holiday'.

- Serif 32px title, e.g. 'Wednesday 14 October'. Sub 'BD10 of October' (plus ' · Fixed Income' after the move).

- Plan rows (48px hours column). Project rows are clickable and open the workspace, and list the task allocation for today and future days.

screens.name: Project workspace
screens.summary:
Single-project screen, layout A from screenshots cp/dp/hv, which the code implements. Padding 22 48 40, flex column, gap 20.

1) Header
- '‹ Projects' back link, domain chip, and an inline-editable project name (14/600; editing it also sets short).
- Hero goal textarea: Libre Caslon 44px/1.12, letter-spacing -0.015em, max 30em, text-wrap balance. Placeholder 'What will be true when this is done?'. It is the view-transition target 'remi-goal'. It is autofocused when a new project is created.

2) Stats strip
- Grid repeat(2,0.9fr) 1.3fr repeat(3,1fr), ink top rule.
- START: a Roll date button that opens the business-day date picker. Sub line '15 BD in of 58' / 'starts in N BD'.
- TARGET: a Roll of targetLabel or targetS. Sub line 'N BD from today' / 'passed'.
- FORECAST: label changes to 'FORECAST THEN' in history. Background tint risk 7% when late. A 'moved +N BD' badge shows for 5.2s after a slip. Contents: a Roll date and a delta chip '+3 BD vs target'. Sub line 'N BD of work left'.
- HOURS A DAY: an input clamped to 0–24 that re-forecasts. Sub line 'averages Xh once BAU days are counted' or 'planned focus time'.
- WORK LEFT: a derived input clamped to 0–999 that re-forecasts.
- TO LAND ON TARGET: a Roll of the needed hours per day. It turns risk-coloured when more than the rate + 0.05.

3) Progress and verdict
- A 3px progress rule filling to elapsed/total in the accent colour.
- Verdict row: a dot and a sentence (5 branches plus suffixes), the confidence meter (5 pills, 12x8), 'Checked in <since>' (risk-coloured when stale), and an outline 'Tell Remi' button.

4) History scrubber
- Grid 200px | 1fr, with 58px top padding.
- Left: 'PLAN AS OF', a Roll date, a hint, and 'Back to now'.
- Bar row (44px): the plan bar, risk overrun, milestone diamonds, end diamond, target flag and today line.
- Hover shows up to 3 rows of packed labels with stems, plus a crosshair tooltip, e.g. 'Mon 19 Oct · BD13 · 3.5h planned · <label>'.
- Track row (44px): month ticks, check-in stops (9px circles) and a 4x21 drag handle. The handle uses pointer capture and snaps to a stop on release.
- While scrubbing, everything interpolates between snapshots. In history mode the body dims to 0.35 and becomes inert.

5) Body (grid 4fr | 8fr, column gap 72)
- Charter:
  - 'Why now' textarea.
  - Success measures (numbered 01, 02), In scope, Out of scope, Constraints. Each list has '+ Add', auto-grow item textareas, and italic empty-state copy.
  - 'Remove project' two-step button (armed state is red for 4s).
- Plan: 'Plan', plus '{est}h estimated in Now' or 'Drafted after the charter'. Three columns 5fr/4fr/3fr:
  - Now ('next 2 weeks · 5–16 Oct'): milestone blocks, each with a diamond, name input, date button, and task rows (15px checkbox, textarea, hours input). '+ Add task', '+ Add milestone'.
  - Next ('2–6 weeks · milestones only'): milestone rows with date buttons.
  - Later: an italic serif line of intent.

Editing rules:
- All inline fields use draft/commit: commit on blur or Enter; Escape reverts; a blank value removes the item.
- Business-day date picker popover, 292px: month grid with 'BD{n}' sub-labels. Picking rolls weekends and holidays forward to the next business day. Has a 'Today' button and a note.

Computed but NOT rendered, although SPEC requires them and the older layout B screenshots show them: phase stepper, exit route, scope log with chart, check-ins timeline, risks (premortem) and checklists.

screens.name: Routines
screens.summary:
Padding 32 48 40. Eyebrow 'Routines'. Title 'What repeats, and where each routine goes next'.

PRIVATE CREDIT section
- Header: dot, 'Private Credit', and '{n} routine(s) on your plan until the move · each one leaves by automation or handover'. Plus an 'Add BAU routine' button.
- Column grid: minmax(0,1.35fr) 110px minmax(0,1.2fr) minmax(0,1.55fr), gap 40. Columns: 'Routine · rule' | 'Effort' | 'Next three' | 'Handover'.
- Each row:
  - Inline name input (20/500).
  - Kind segmented control: Monthly | Weekly | Daily.
  - Monthly shows a BD stepper '− BD3 +' (range 1–20). Weekly shows a Mon–Fri picker.
  - Rule sentence, e.g. '3rd business day, monthly · 12 funds'.
  - Effort: auto-width hours input (24px) + 'h', 'per run', and a monthly estimate '6h a month' / '≈4.3h a month' / '≈21h a month'.
  - Next three: a 4x34 tick (filled when the run is today), the date, and 'today' / '{n} BD away' / 'after the move'.
  - Handover stepper: Manual → Automating → Shadowed → Handed over, each with a 9px dot. Changing it logs a feed item.
  - Handover note textarea, placeholder 'Where does this routine go after the move?'.
  - 'Via <Project> · <forecast>' link.
  - Two-step 'Remove'.
- Hovering a row dims the other rows to 0.35.
- Deep link from Today's 'Routine ↗': scrolls to the row with a 120px offset and flashes a pc-accent 8% tint for 1600ms.

FIXED INCOME section
- Header subtitle: 'Eurozone sovereign rotation · 4h a day from the move · one country at a time, then round again'.
- Read-only racetrack, 328px tall with 120px gutters:
  - Stadium outline: 2px, fi-accent 35%, radius 999.
  - Two rows of 5 tiles (112px tall, 28px gap): top row 01–05, bottom row reversed 10–06, with chevrons showing clockwise flow.
  - Tile 01 has an ink border, the flag 'First up · Mon 4 Jan' and 'Refresh 9 Mar – 11 Mar'.
  - 'Now' label: 'Waiting to start. 61 BD to go.'
  - Middle stats: 'Loop 1: 10 countries · 46 business days' | 'Estimated completion: Mon 8 Mar 2027' | 'Then: Back to Germany to refresh, Tue 9 Mar – 11 Mar'.
- Legend: Build / Refresh.
- Hovering the FI block sets hover 'rot'.

screens.name: Transition

Answers 'Am I on track to move cleanly?'. Padding 36 48 48, flex column, gap 40.

1) Hero (grid 5fr | 7fr, gap 72)
- Left: eyebrow 'Transition'; a huge '61' (120px, weight 300, line-height 0.9, letter-spacing -0.04em); 'business days to Fixed Income' / 'Monday 4 January 2027'.
- Right: eyebrow 'Am I on track to move cleanly?'; a 10px dot plus verdict.short at 36/600 ('Yes' / 'Yes, narrowly' / 'At risk' / 'Not yet'); the verdict sentence at 17px muted.

2) Business-day strip
- Flag lane, 44px:
  - PC forecast flags '<short> · D Mon', drawn in risk colour when late.
  - 'Dec run' in muted.
  - 'Move' in fi-accent, right-aligned.
  - Sticks alternate between low (10px) and high (26px) by sorted index.
  - Flags move with a 440ms spring on 'left'.

- Month labels.
- Legend.

3) Two columns (1fr 1fr, gap 72)
PRIVATE CREDIT 'wind down':
- Group 'Wind-down projects · N projects'. Rows (grid 1fr 170px 150px) show the name, a readiness bar with %, the forecast 'D Mon' and a delta chip. Clicking opens the workspace; hovering dims the others to 0.35.

screens.name: Tell Remi check-in drawer
screens.summary:
Sits on a full-app overlay layer (z 20) with an ink 18% scrim.
- Panel: 1160px wide (max calc(100% - 160px)), paper background, hairline left border, shadow -24px 0 48px -32px ink 30%.
- Slides between translateX(104%) and 0 over 440ms spring, with opacity over 240ms.
- Stays mounted. Its state resets on every open (session counter).

Layout: rows 84px header | body | 76px footer.
- Header: 'Tell Remi' (22/600), the subtitle 'Say what happened in your own words. Remi works out what to change and shows you before anything moves.', and a close button.
- Body: grid 1fr | 500px.

Left column:
- Focus chip: soft accent, 'About <project name>', with an x to clear it. Without a focus: 'About anything: mention projects or routines by name'.
- Large serif 22px/1.55 textarea on paper-raised, with a placeholder example. It is locked at 0.6 opacity while thinking. Focus border uses --focus. It autofocuses at 380ms.
- Hint line: word count or instruction.
- 'Send to Remi ⌘↵' button, shown in compose only.

Right column, one of four phases:
- COMPOSE: 'Remi can', a 6-row capability list (140px key, italic serif example), and a footnote.
- THINKING: 'Reading your update' / 'a few seconds'. A 2px bar goes 0→88% over 2600ms with cubic-bezier(0.2,0.7,0.3,1). Echo quotes (up to 5 sentences) stagger in 180ms apart.
- REVIEW:
  - 'Remi will change' plus 'simple reading' or '<n> of <total> selected'. A 19px serif summary.
  - Groups per project (or 'BAU · today') with an ink rule, a dot, the name, and an EffectChip showing the forecast impact live from the accepted rows.
  - Toggleable rows (26 | 104 | 1fr): checkbox, KIND label, text. Rows that are off get a strike-through and opacity 0.55.

engineAlgorithms.name: Day numbers and formatters
engineAlgorithms.spec:
Day numbers:
- dn(iso) = round(Date.UTC(y, m-1, d) / 86400000), i.e. UTC days since the epoch. dn('2026-10-05') = 20731, a Monday.
- isoOf(n) = new Date(n*86400000).toISOString().slice(0,10).
- Weekday = getUTCDay() (0 = Sun).

Formatters:
- F.s(n) = WDS[w] + ' ' + d + ' ' + MOS[m], e.g. 'Mon 5 Oct'.
- F.dm(n) = '5 Oct'.
- F.l(n) = 'Monday 5 October'.
- F.wd = 'Mon'; F.mon = 'Oct'; F.monL = 'October'; F.d = 5.
- ORD(n) = n + ('st' if n%10===1 && n!==11; 'nd' if 2 && !12; 'rd' if 3 && !13; else 'th').
- hrs(h) = round(h×100)/100 + 'h'.
- hr(x) rounds to 1 decimal.

Display conventions:
- The minus sign is U+2212 '−' in delta labels.
- Date ranges use an en dash with spaces: 'A – B'. The week label uses an unspaced en dash: '5–9 Oct'.

Production:
- Canonical API dates are ISO strings.
- 'Today' is a business-timezone calendar date, or Settings.todayOverride when set.
- Formatters need a year variant for ranges that span years.

engineAlgorithms.name: Business-day calendar
engineAlgorithms.outputs: days map, bds[], idx, nextBD, addBD, bdDiff, bdm
engineAlgorithms.spec:
Build a record for every day n in the range: {n, iso, w, m, d, y, bd, bdm, hol}.
- bd = w in 1..5 && no holiday.
- bdm = running count of business days within the calendar month (1-based, resets when the month changes); null on non-business days.
- hol = holiday name or null.
- bds = ascending array of business days. idx[n] = position of n in bds.

Operations:
- nextBD(n): step forward while days[n] exists and is not a business day.
- addBD(n, k) = bds[clamp(idx[nextBD(n)] + k, 0, len-1)]. k may be negative. It silently clamps at the ends of the range.
- bdDiff(a, b) = idx[nextBD(b)] - idx[nextBD(a)]. Non-business inputs roll forward first. Outside the range it returns NaN.

Prototype range: 2026-08-31..2027-04-30, which has 170 business days.
- Monthly counts: Oct 22, Nov 21, Dec 21 (25 and 28 Dec are holidays), Jan 20, Feb 20, Mar 21, Apr 22.
- bdDiff(TODAY, MOVE) = 62.
- Business days strictly between Mon 5 Oct and Mon 4 Jan = 61, which is the '61' in the UI.

Production:
- Generate the range dynamically, or lazily extend it by year.
- Raise a typed error or extend the range instead of clamping or crashing.
- Unit-test with Vitest.
- Also provide ISO-8601 week numbers: shift to the Thursday of the week, then 1 + round((thu - jan4Thursday) / 7 days).

engineAlgorithms.name: Routine occurrence, rule text and effort
engineAlgorithms.spec:
occurs(r, d) = d exists && d.bd && ANY of:
- r.kind === 'daily';
- r.kind === 'weekly' && d.w === r.wd;
- r.kind is 'monthly' (or missing) && d.bdm === r.bd.
A monthly routine whose bd is larger than the month's business-day count never fires that month; there is no clamp.

Text:
- ruleText: 'Every business day' | 'Every ' + full weekday name | ORD(bd) + ' business day, monthly'.
- ruleShort: 'Daily' | 'Weekly · ' + short weekday | 'BD' + bd.

Next occurrences:
- next = the first 3 business days n >= TODAY where occurs(r, n) is true, each as {n, s: F.s(n), after: n >= MOVE, today: n === TODAY}.
- This ignores stage, so handed-over routines still list dates.
- 'n BD away' = bdDiff(TODAY, n).

Monthly effort estimate:
- daily: '≈' + round(h×21) + 'h a month'.
- weekly: '≈' + round(h×4.3×10)/10 + 'h a month'.
- monthly: h + 'h a month', with no ≈.

nextRunAfter(S) (the NoBau copy):
- The earliest date in any routine's next[] that is greater than S. Otherwise 'after the move'.
- Production should compute this from S, not from the 3 dates counted from today.

engineAlgorithms.name: FI rotation schedule
engineAlgorithms.inputs: segments [country, code, lengthBD, pass], startDate = MOVE
engineAlgorithms.outputs: segments with s, e, sS, eS; loopBD; loopEnd; refresh
engineAlgorithms.spec:
Layout:
- Start with s = MOVE.
- For each segment in order: e = addBD(s, len-1); record {i, country, code, len, pass, s, e, sS: F.s(s), eS: F.s(e)}; then s = addBD(e, 1).
- Segments run back to back in business days and skip holidays.
- Total length is 49 BD, ending Thu 11 Mar 2027.

Derived values:
- loopBD = Σ len of the Build passes = 46.
- loopEnd = the last Build segment's eS, 'Mon 8 Mar'. The prototype hard-codes ROT[9] and appends ' 2027'.
- refresh = ROT[10]: 'Tue 9 Mar – 11 Mar'.
- currentSegment = the segment containing today, or 'Waiting to start. N BD to go.' before the move.

In dayLoad, each business day inside a segment carries BAU {id:'rot', domain:'fi', h: hoursPerDay (4), name: country + ' · ' + pass}.

engineAlgorithms.name: dayLoad (capacity per business day)
engineAlgorithms.inputs: n, derived projects, routines, rotation, settings
engineAlgorithms.outputs: DayLoad {n, items, bau, proj, total, free, over}
engineAlgorithms.spec:
Return null if n is not a business day.

BAU:
- If n < MOVE: for each routine with stage < 3 where occurs(r, day) is true, push {id: r.id, pid: r.pid, kind:'bau', domain: 'pc', h: +r.h || 0, name: r.short || r.name || 'Untitled routine'}.
  - The domain is hard-coded to 'pc'; production should use r.domain.
  - The hours come from the routine.
- Otherwise (n >= MOVE): all routines are ignored. If n falls inside a rotation segment, push {id:'rot', pid:'rot', kind:'bau', domain:'fi', h: 4, name: country + ' · ' + pass}.

Projects, in project order:
- end = forecastN ?? targetN. Skip the project if n < startN or n > end.
- Hours, first match wins:
  1. ov[iso] (explicit override, even 0);
  2. n >= MOVE → rateAfter || 0;
  3. bdm === 3 → bd3;
  4. bdm === 8 → bd8;
  5. rate.
- Push {id, pid, kind:'proj', domain, h, name: p.short} only if h > 0.

Totals:
- bau = Σ BAU hours; proj = Σ project hours; total = bau + proj.
- free = max(0, CAP - total).
- over = total > CAP, strictly greater. CAP = 8.

Seed checks:
- Mon 5 Oct (BD3): Returns 6 + ManCo 2 = 8h, 0 free.
- Ordinary October/November day: ret 3.5 + manco 1.5 + play 1 + fion 1 = 7h.
- Mon 12 Oct (BD8): ManCo pack 4 + ret 2 + manco 1.5 + play 0.5 = 8h.
- Wed 4 Nov (BD3): Returns 6 + ret override 3.5 = 9.5h, over. This is the only overload in the range.
- Mon 4 Jan: Germany · Build 4 + fion 1 + alpha 3 = 8h.

Production:
- Replace the hard-coded bd3/bd8 hooks with a general 'reduced project hours on routine days' mechanism.
- Count FI routines after the move.
- Make hours per day, rotation hours and capacity (from Settings, minus leave) configurable.
- Memoise the result. The prototype recomputes 170 days × all projects on every render.

engineAlgorithms.name: Project derivation and derivedMs
engineAlgorithms.spec:
Numbers and status:
- startN, targetN, forecastN (null if no forecast), prevN.
- delta = forecastN != null ? bdDiff(targetN, forecastN) : null.
- status = forecastN == null ? 'define' : delta > 0 ? 'risk' : 'on'. Being early counts as 'on'.
- since = checkin ? TODAY - dn(checkin) : null, in CALENDAR days.
- stale = since != null && since >= 7.
- added = Σ scope.h. growth = baseline ? round(added/baseline×100) : 0.

Labels:
- deltaLabel = null → 'No forecast'; > 0 → '+N BD'; < 0 → '−N BD'; 0 → 'On target'.
- sinceLabel = 'Not yet' | 'Today' | 'Yesterday' | 'N days ago'.
- forecastS = F.s or 'Not yet'. forecastDM = F.dm or '—'.
- targetS = targetLabel || F.s. targetDM = targetLabel || F.dm.
- statusColor: risk → var(--risk); define → var(--ink-faint); otherwise the domain accent.

derivedMs(p):
1. Put every now[] and next[] entry that has both m and due into a Map keyed by name, as {name: m, date: due}. A later entry with the same name overwrites an earlier one.
2. Add each explicit p.milestones entry only if its name is not already in the map AND its date is not already used.
3. Sort by ISO date ascending.
A milestone is 'passed' when date < TODAY. Production should key milestones by id.

engineAlgorithms.name: Move verdict
engineAlgorithms.inputs: derived projects, MOVE, key project, key run date
engineAlgorithms.outputs: Verdict {word, short, dot, sentence, buffer, toRun}
engineAlgorithms.spec:
Inputs:
- pcP = PC projects. lastPC = max(forecastN). Null coerces to 0; guard against this in production.
- buffer = bdDiff(lastPC, MOVE). This counts the move day, so the seed gives 8, while the Transition strip shows 7 hollow blocks.
- ret = pmap[keyProjectId] (hard-coded 'ret').
- toRun = bdDiff(ret.forecastN, DEC_RUN). DEC_RUN = 2026-12-03, the last r-ret occurrence before the move.

Rules, evaluated in order:
1. Any PC forecastN >= MOVE:
   - word 'Off track for the move'; short 'Not yet'; dot var(--overload).
   - sentence 'A Private Credit exit now lands on or after 4 Jan. Something has to be cut, automated later, or handed over as it stands.'
2. Else, ret.forecastN >= DEC_RUN:
   - word 'Move at risk'; short 'At risk'; dot var(--risk).
   - sentence 'Every Private Credit exit still lands before 4 Jan, but the returns pipeline now misses the December run on Thu 3 Dec, the last one your successor can shadow with you there.'
3. Else:
   - word 'Move on track, narrowly' / short 'Yes, narrowly' if ANY project (any domain) has status 'risk'; otherwise 'Move on track' / 'Yes'. dot var(--ink).
   - sentence 'Every Private Credit exit lands before 4 Jan, with {buffer} business days to spare. The one to watch is the returns pipeline: forecast {ret.forecastS}, {toRun} business day(s) before the December run your successor needs to shadow.'

Seed result: narrowly, buffer 8, toRun 1.

Production:
- Use a configurable key project, key routine and key run.
- Format dates from the move date.
- Handle the key project being missing and the case of no PC projects.

engineAlgorithms.name: Flags: upcoming overloads, attention, check-in prompt
engineAlgorithms.spec:
upcoming:
- Business days n with TODAY <= n <= addBD(MOVE, 10) and loads[n].over.
- Each as {n, s, bdm, total}.

attention, in this order:
(a) Each risk project: {id:'a-'+id, pid, kind:'At risk', title: name, body: 'Forecast ' + forecastS + ', target ' + targetS, chip: deltaLabel, tone: 'risk'}.
(b) Each upcoming overload: {id:'o-'+n, day: n, kind:'Overload', title: s + ' (BD' + bdm + ')', body: total + 'h of an 8h day', chip: '+' + (total-8) + 'h', tone: 'overload'}.
(c) Each stale project: {id:'s-'+id, kind:'Stale', title: name, body: 'No check-in for ' + since + ' days', chip: since + 'd', tone: 'quiet'}.

Prompt:
- candidates = projects with since != null, sorted by since descending.
- prompt = candidates[0] if it is stale, otherwise null.
- nextDue = candidates[0].

Seed: attention = [At risk Returns pipeline +3 BD, Overload Wed 4 Nov (BD3) +1.5h, Stale ManCo 9d]; prompt = manco.

SPEC also defines 'overload' as BAU alone exceeding capacity on a day, or the week total exceeding capacity. Reconcile with the per-day rule used here.

engineAlgorithms.name: Workspace forecast maths (dayH, workBetween, finishFor, refit)
engineAlgorithms.outputs: hours per day, work totals, forecast date, updated project
engineAlgorithms.spec:
dayH(p, n, rate):
- 0 if n is not a business day.
- k = p.rate ? rate/p.rate : 1.
- Otherwise, first match wins: ov[iso]×k; if n >= MOVE, (rateAfter||0)×k; if bdm 3, (bd3||0)×k; if bdm 8, (bd8||0)×k; else rate.

workBetween(p, a, b, rate) = Σ dayH over business days a..b inclusive.

finishFor(p, from, hours, rate):
- If hours <= 0, return nextBD(from).
- Otherwise walk business days from 'from', accumulating dayH, and return the first n where the sum >= hours - 0.01.
- If the calendar runs out, it returns the last business day, a silent clamp.

Work left: from = max(TODAY, startN); left = forecastN != null ? round(workBetween(p, from, forecastN, p.rate)×2)/2 : null. It is derived, never stored.

refit(raw, fields, rate, hours, start):
1. kk = p.rate ? rate/p.rate : 1.
2. If the rate changed, multiply bd3, bd8, rateAfter and every ov value by kk.
3. If hours == null or rate <= 0, return the rate and field changes only, leaving the forecast untouched.
4. Otherwise nf = finishFor(merged project, max(TODAY, start), hours, rate). Set forecast = iso(nf) and prev = (raw.forecast && raw.forecast !== iso(nf)) ? raw.forecast : raw.prev.

Uses:
- Rate edit: refit(rate = new, hours = left, start = startN).
- Work-left edit: refit(rate = raw.rate || 1, hours = new), which also saves rate 1 if it was 0.
- Start edit: refit(fields {start}, rate = raw.rate || 0, hours = left, start = new).
None of these edits logs feed or a check-in.

engineAlgorithms.name: Workspace panel metrics and verdict sentence
engineAlgorithms.spec:
Metrics:
- from = max(TODAY, startN); started = startN <= TODAY; hasF = forecastN != null.
- bdLeft = hasF ? max(0, bdDiff(from, forecastN)+1) : null.
- bdTgt = targetN >= from ? bdDiff(from, targetN)+1 : 0.
- capTgt = workBetween(p, from, targetN, rate).
- need = left != null && bdTgt > 0 ? left/bdTgt : null. This is a flat average and ignores BD3/BD8/override days, so it can print 'plan 3.5h a day instead of 3.5h'. Production should solve for k such that workBetween(from, target, k) = left.
- avgPlan = left/bdLeft. The 'averages Xh once BAU days are counted' sub shows when |avgPlan - rate| > 0.2.
- buffer = hasF ? bdDiff(forecastN, targetN) : null.
- total = hasF ? bdDiff(startN, forecastN)+1 : 0. done = started ? max(0, bdDiff(startN, TODAY)) : 0. progress = min(100, done/total×100).
- overDays = business days in [from, forecastN] where loads[n].over and this project is among the items.
- needBad = need > rate + 0.05.

Sentence, first match wins:
(1) No forecast: 'No plan yet. Enter the work left and hours a day, and Remi works out when it lands.' (ink-faint).
(2) PC and forecastN >= MOVE: 'Lands after the move on 4 Jan. At {rate}h a day this does not leave with you; cut {max(0, left - workBetween(from, addBD(MOVE,-1)))}h or plan more time.' (overload).
(3) buffer < 0: 'Lands {-buffer} BD after target. To make {targetS}, plan {need}h a day instead of {rate}h, or cut about {max(0, left - capTgt)}h of work.' (risk).
(4) buffer === 0: 'No buffer. It lands on the target day, so any new scope pushes it past {targetS}.' (risk).
(5) Otherwise: '{buffer} BD of buffer: roughly {workBetween(addBD(forecastN,1), targetN)}h of new scope before the target moves.' (ink).

Appended when they apply:
- ' It sits on {k} overloaded day{s}, first {F.s(overDays[0])}.'
- ' Not checked in for {since} days, so treat the forecast as untested.'
- ' Starts in {bdDiff(TODAY, startN)} BD.'

Plan note: status define → 'Drafted after the charter'; otherwise '{Σ hours of undone Now tasks, 2dp}h estimated in Now'.

engineAlgorithms.name: Check-in apply (applyUpdate + applyCheckIn) as ONE transaction
engineAlgorithms.inputs: accepted Change[] (and optional raw text, focus)
engineAlgorithms.outputs: updated projects, tasks, feed, BAU runs, movements
engineAlgorithms.spec:
Change union:
- task_done {project_id, task_id}
- task_add {project_id, text, hours}
- scope_add {project_id, text, hours}
- blocker {project_id, text}
- confidence {project_id, value}
- target_move {project_id, date}
- hours_per_day {project_id, value}
- note {project_id, text}
- bau_done {routine_id}

Phase A: group changes by project_id. For each project p0:
1. pre.target = the date of the LAST target_move.
2. hpd = the first hours_per_day with value > 0.
   - If p0 has a forecast:
     - from = max(TODAY, dn(start)); bdLeft = bdDiff(from, forecast)+1.
     - left = (rate||1)×bdLeft; need = max(1, ceil(left/hpd.value)).
     - k = rate ? hpd.value/rate : 1.
     - pre gets rate = hpd.value, bd3×k, bd8×k, rateAfter×k, forecast = iso(addBD(from, need-1)), prev = old forecast.
   - Otherwise only rate = hpd.value.
3. adds = task_add changes that have text. Append each to now[0].tasks as {id, t: text, h: +hours || 1}. If there is no Now milestone, first create {m:'Added from an update', due: addBD(TODAY, 9), tasks: []}.
4. If the target changed, delete targetLabel.
5. If hpd changed the forecast, raise flash[pid] for 1100ms.

Phase B: ALWAYS run applyCheckIn against the UPDATED project (new rate and forecast):
- done = task_done ids.
- changed = note texts with any trailing '.' stripped, joined with '. '.
- scopeWhat = scope texts joined with ', '. scopeH = Σ scope hours.
- blockers = the FIRST blocker text, or ''.
- confidence = the first confidence value, or null.

applyCheckIn(d):
- hasF = project has a forecast.
- slip = hasF && scopeH > 0 ? ceil(scopeH/(rate||1)) : 0. This uses the flat rate only.
- newF = slip ? addBD(fN, slip) : fN.
- what = trim(scopeWhat) || 'New scope'.
- note = [changed, scopeH > 0 ? what + ' added, +' + scopeH + 'h' : '', blockers ? 'Blocked: ' + blockers : ''] filtered and joined with '. ', or 'Plan confirmed.' if empty.
- Project updates:
  - forecast = newF; prev = slip ? old forecast : old prev (this overrides the prev set by the hpd step);
  - confidence = d.confidence ?? old; checkin = TODAY;
  - blocker = d.blockers || null (every check-in overwrites or clears it);
  - if scopeH > 0, append a scope entry {date TODAY, what, h, bd: slip, from, to};
  - always append a checkin {date, note, forecast, conf}. Production should also store the milestone snapshot, target and raw text.
- Mark done tasks as done. Production must also set doneAt; the prototype doesn't.
- Feed item:
  - if slip: {kind:'scope', tone:'risk', title: short, body: 'Scope added (' + what.toLowerCase() + ', +' + h + 'h). Forecast moved ' + dm(fN) + ' → ' + dm(newF) + '.', delta: '+N BD'};
  - otherwise: {kind:'checkin', tone:'quiet', body: 'Checked in. ' + (changed ? changed + '. ' : '') + (hasF ? 'Forecast holds at ' + dm(fN) + '.' : ''), delta: '±0 BD'}.
  - Prepend it, and remove this project's 'stale' feed items.
- Transient UI: flash = !!slip for 1100ms; moved = slip ? {delta, label: '+N BD', at} : null for 5200ms. A new check-in on the same project resets both timers.

Phase C, for each bau_done:
- If the routine has a run checklist (r-ret) and it occurs today, tick every item for today's run.
- Otherwise record RoutineRun(routineId, today).

Production:
- Execute all phases in ONE DB transaction.
- Return movements [{projectId, from, to, deltaBD, cause}] so the client can play flash and moved.
- The client waits 220ms after the drawer closes before animating.
- Don't rely on synchronous setState ordering; the prototype does.

engineAlgorithms.name: Check-in preview (EffectChip) and previewShift
engineAlgorithms.inputs: accepted changes per project; or (pid, hours)
engineAlgorithms.spec:
EffectChip, computed only if forecastN != null, from the ACCEPTED rows in the group:
- h = Σ scope_add hours; rc = first hours_per_day; tg = first target_move.
- to = forecastN.
- If rc: from = max(TODAY, startN); left = rate×(bdDiff(from, forecastN)+1); to = addBD(from, max(1, ceil(left/rc.value)) - 1).
- If h: to = addBD(to, ceil(h/((rc ? rc.value : rate) || 1))).
- tgt = tg ? dn(tg.date) : targetN.
- d = bdDiff(forecastN, to); late = to > tgt.
- d !== 0 → text 'D Mon → D Mon · ±N BD'. When late: background risk 22%/paper, text risk 40%/ink. Otherwise outlined, ink-muted, hairline.
- d === 0 with a target move → 'forecast holds', or 'now N BD past target' when late.
- Otherwise no chip.
It must use exactly the same maths as apply. The prototype differs when rate is 0: preview uses rate, apply uses rate||1.

previewShift(pid, h):
- delta = h > 0 ? ceil(h/(rate||1)) : 0; to = addBD(forecastN, delta).
- newOver = business days in (forecastN, to] that become over with the extended project and were not over before.
- Returns {delta, from, to, fromS, toS, fromDM, toDM, deltaLabel ('+N BD'|'±0 BD'), vsTarget: bdDiff(targetN, to), newOver: [{n, s, total}], missesKeyRun: pid is the key project && to >= keyRun, crossesMove: pc && to >= MOVE}.
- Seed: ret +6h → +2 BD, 2 Dec → Fri 4 Dec, new overload Fri 4 Dec at 9h, misses the key run.
This is the input for the structured check-in live preview.

engineAlgorithms.name: Focus-block / day task allocation (Today and Calendar)
engineAlgorithms.inputs: project, day S, loads, task done map
engineAlgorithms.spec:
Steps:
1. all = p.now.flatMap(ms => ms.tasks).
   - On a future day, drop tasks that are already done.
   - On today, keep done tasks. This is a quirk: tasks done on earlier days still consume today's hours. Production should keep tasks done today and drop tasks done earlier.
2. off = 0 on today. Otherwise off = Σ of this project's planned hours on business days TODAY <= n < S.
3. Walk the tasks cumulatively. Task i covers [a0, a1) with a1 = a0 + (+t.h || 0).
4. Include a task if a1 > off + 0.01 and a0 < off + dayHours - 0.01.

Empty copy:
- No Now tasks at all: 'No tasks planned in Now yet. Add them in the workspace.'
- None left in the window: 'The tasks in Now are used up before this day. Plan the next ones in the workspace.'

Calendar shows the allocation only when S >= TODAY.

Next milestone line:
- The first entry of [...now, ...next] with due >= S, sorted by ISO.
- Label: 'Milestone due this day: ' or 'Next milestone: ' + name + ' · ' + F.s(due).

Seed (today, ManCo, 2h): man-0 0.5h, man-1 0.75h, man-2 0.75h.

engineAlgorithms.name: Today month snapshot
engineAlgorithms.spec:
Setup: take the business days of TODAY's month. mStart = the first, mEnd = the last.

BAU rows:
- For each routine with stage < 3, and each business day n in the month where n < MOVE and occurs(r, n):
  - key = routineId:iso.
  - done: for a checklist routine on today, every item ticked; otherwise a run completion exists. doneOn = the completion date.
  - text = name + (monthly ? '' : ' · ' + dm(n)). sub = 'BD' + bdm. due = n.

Project rows (projects with a forecast):
- Every Now task whose (t.due || ms.due) <= mEnd. There is no lower bound, so earlier overdue tasks are included.
- Every NEXT milestone with due <= mEnd, as '◆ name'.
- sub = short.

Counts:
- total = rows; doneN = done rows; lateN = not done && due < TODAY.

Cumulative bars, for each business day index i:
- plan = count(due <= n).
- dn = past ? count(done && doneOn <= n) : 0.
- late = past ? count(due < n && !(done && doneOn <= n)) : 0.
- Heights: outline = plan/total, late layer = (dn + late)/total, done layer = dn/total. All are 0% before arrival.
- The late and done layers stagger by i×8ms.
- Tooltip: 'Mon 5 Oct · 3 due by then, 2 done, 1 overdue'.

Row due label:
- 'done D Mon' | 'overdue N BD' (bdDiff(due, TODAY)) | 'today' | F.s(due).

Groups (BAU limit 4, Projects limit 5):
- Open rows sorted by due ascending; done rows by doneOn descending.
- Collapsed shows the first `limit` open rows. Expanded shows all open, then all done.
- more = 'Show {hidden} more and {done} done' | 'Show less'.
- empty = 'Nothing due this month.' | 'All done for the month.'

Seed: '2 of 17 done · 1 overdue'.

engineAlgorithms.name: Timeline geometry
engineAlgorithms.inputs: window [T0, T1] or 2-week window, measured width W, zoom
engineAlgorithms.outputs: slot x positions, Lx/Rx/Cx, month/week labels
engineAlgorithms.spec:
Slots:
- Iterate T0..T1. Each business day is a slot {t:'bd', a:n, b:n}.
- Each run of consecutive non-business days collapses into one {t:'gap', a:first, b:last}.
- Gap width s = 5px in 3m, 18px in 2w.

Window:
- 3m: winA = T0, winB = T1.
- 2w: winA = Monday of today's week + wk×7; winB = winA + 13.
- vis = slots fully inside the window. nbd = BD slots in vis; ng = gap slots in vis.

Positions:
- Column width w = max(4, (W - ng×s)/max(1, nbd)).
- Give every slot a cumulative x. off = vis[0].x in 2w, 0 in 3m.
- Lx(n) = left edge of the slot for nextBD(n), minus off. Values before T0 map to -off-40; after T1 to total-off+40.
- Rx(n) = right edge. After T1 it maps to total-off+80.
- Cx = (Lx + Rx)/2.

Labels:
- Month labels span all slots: x = max(0, x0), width clamped to W, opacity 1 if width > 70. Label is the full month name, plus the year for January and for the first month.
- Weeks: an ISO-week label at the first business day of each week.

Capacity strip: 5px per hour; bar width max(3, min(colW - 5, 30)).

Project geometry:
- a = Lx(startN).
- Bar width = (risk ? Rx(target) : Rx(forecast ?? target)) - a.
- Overrun from Rx(target) to Rx(forecast).
- Ghost from a to Rx(prevN).
- Milestone diamonds at Cx - 5.
- End diamond at Rx(end) - 7.
- Target marker at Rx(target); hidden for Define projects or targets past T1.
- Moved chip at Rx(forecast) + 10.

Stagger: rows i×30 + 60ms (FI offset by PC count); rotation segments 200 + i×20ms; capacity columns round(i×2.5)ms. After 900ms (settled) all delays become 0.

BAU tick width: 4px in 3m, max(4, colW - 10) in 2w.

Tooltip positioning: k = offsetWidth/rect.width (to undo scale). x = cursor + 16, flipped by -332 if x + 310 > width. y = cursor + 16, flipped by -150 if y + 140 > height.

Production: derive T0/T1 from today and the move date (e.g. Monday of the previous week through MOVE + 2 weeks), not hard-coded dates.

engineAlgorithms.name: Transition strip and flags
engineAlgorithms.inputs: TODAY, MOVE, PC projects, key run
engineAlgorithms.spec:
Remaining days:
- rem = business days n with TODAY < n < MOVE. N = rem.length = 61 in the seed.

Ticks:
- A tick is filled pc-accent-soft with a pc-accent 55% outline if n <= lastPC, otherwise hollow with a hairline outline.
- Title: F.s(n) + ' · BD' + bdm.

Positions (these ignore the 2px gaps between ticks):
- pos(n) = (index of the first rem >= n, or N)/N × 100%.
- posEnd(n) = the same with '> n'.

Flags:
- Each PC project with a forecast: x = posEnd(forecastN), label short + ' · ' + forecastDM, colour risk 45%/ink if at risk else ink.
- 'Dec run': x = pos(DEC_RUN), ink-muted.
- 'Move': x = 100%, fi-accent, right-aligned via translateX(-100%).
- Sort by x; the sort is stable.
- Odd sorted index: label lifted 18px with a 26px stick. Even: lifted 2px with a 10px stick.
- Seed: ret 68.852%, Dec run 68.852%, manco 80.328%, play 88.525%. Note ret and Dec run overlap.

Month marks: at k/N wherever the month changes, labelled with the full month name.

Project row:
- readiness% = round(readiness × 100).
- Chip in risk tint if at risk.
- Hovering dims the other rows to 0.35.

Onboarding count: '{done} of {total} ready'.

Rotation tiles: ROT[0..2], each 'D Mon – D Mon', with the first tile emphasised.

engineAlgorithms.name: History scrubber (snapshots and interpolation)
engineAlgorithms.spec:
Snapshots:
- snaps = checkins.map(c => {date: dn(c.date), f: dn(forecast) | null, conf, ms: (c.ms || current milestones) as {name, n}}).
- If there are no check-ins, snaps = [current].
- Otherwise the last snapshot is replaced with {current live state, date: lastCheckin.date}.

Axis:
- A0 = min(startN, snapshot dates) - 4.
- A1 = max(targetN > TODAY + 200 ? TODAY + 120 : targetN, TODAY, all snapshot forecasts) + 12.
- pct(n) = clamp01((n - A0)/(A1 - A0)) × 100%.
- Stop x positions: xs[i] = (date - A0)/(A1 - A0) × 100.

Interpolation for pos in [0, last]:
- i0 = floor(pos); t = pos - i0; i1 = min(last, i0 + 1).
- fNow = lerp(A.f, B.f, t). risk = fNow > targetN + 0.5.
- Plan bar from pct(startN) to pct(min(fNow, targetN) + 1). Overrun from pct(targetN + 1) to pct(fNow + 1).
- Milestones use the union of names. If a name is in both snapshots, lerp its date. Opacity = (inA ? 1 - t : 0) + (inB ? t : 0).
- End diamond at pct(fNow + 0.5); target at pct(targetN + 1); today at pct(TODAY + 0.5).
- near = snaps[round(pos)] supplies the confidence and the 'Plan as of' date.

Pointer to pos:
- Piecewise linear between stops.
- On release, round. If the result is the last stop, pos = null (live).

Hover labels:
- Start, milestones, forecast ('{endName} · forecast') and Target.
- Estimated width = len×6.1 + dateLen×6.2 + 34.
- Anchor: left if xp < 6%, right if xp > 94%, else centred.
- Greedy packing into 3 rows at 17px pitch.

Crosshair text: F.s(n) + (' · BD' + bdm | ' · ' + holiday | ' · weekend') + (' · ' + dayH + 'h planned' when startN <= n <= fNow) + (' · ' + label on that day).

Production: store full snapshots, including the target, so the history delta compares against the target that applied at the time.

engineAlgorithms.name: Calendar month grid and day panel
engineAlgorithms.spec:
Grid range:
- first = the 1st of the month. start = first - ((w(first) + 6) % 7), i.e. Monday-based.
- end = last day of the month + (6 - ((w(last) + 6) % 7)).
- Cells run start..end (35 or 42). inMonth = same month AND same year; the prototype compares month only.

Cell content (in-month business days only):
- BAU chips: '{name} · {h}h'.
- Milestones dated that day. Fill is the accent if the day is past, otherwise paper.
- Forecast ends: '{short} · {endName lowercased}', in risk colour if at risk.
- Project bars: width h/8 × 62%, red if the day is over.
- Load meter: cap = max(total, 8); segments calc(h/cap×100% - 1px); plus a free segment.

Month sub-line: nBD + ' business days' + (overN ? ' · ' + overN + ' overloaded' : '').

Panel kicker:
- 'Today' | 'Weekend' | 'Bank holiday'.
- Otherwise from ahead = bdDiff(TODAY, sel): 'N business day(s) ago', 'Tomorrow' (ahead === 1, in business days), or 'N business days ahead'.

Panel sub: 'BD{bdm} of {Month}' (+ ' · Fixed Income' if on or after MOVE) | holiday name | 'Not a business day'.

Due list:
- milestones '{name} · {short}';
- forecast ends '{short} · {endName} (forecast)';
- targets '{short} · target';
- 'Move to Fixed Income' on MOVE.

Panel capacity label: '{t}h of 8h · {free}h free' | '{t}h planned · {t-8}h over'.

step(k): move to the adjacent business day. It switches month only within the displayed range.

Open-in-Today is allowed when the day is a business day and on or after TODAY.

engineAlgorithms.name: Command palette search
engineAlgorithms.spec:
Setup: q = trimmed, lower-cased query. hm = q.match(/\+?\s*(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*h\b/).

Quick add (when hm matches):
- h = parseFloat(hm[1]). rest = q with the match removed, trimmed.
- For each project with a forecast whose (name + ' ' + short) lower-cased includes rest (or all such projects if rest is empty): {group 'Quick add', label 'Add {h}h of scope to {short}', hint 'check-in', dot accent, run openCheckIn(id, {scopeH: h})}.
- No other groups appear in quick-add mode.

Otherwise, in this order:
- Jump to: screens whose label includes q (all if q is empty). Dot hairline, empty hint.
- Projects: name includes q. Hint forecastS.
- Tell Remi: ('check in ' + name) includes q. Label 'Tell Remi about {short}', hint sinceLabel. Note that typing 'tell' matches nothing here; fix this.
- Create: 'New Private Credit project' and 'New Fixed Income project', shown if q is empty, the label includes q, or 'new project'.includes(q).
- 'Reset to sample data' (hint 'clears your edits'): only when q is non-empty and 'reset sample data'.includes(q). This should be dev-only.

Truncate to 16 items. sel = min(i, len - 1).

With an empty query the list is 7 Jump to + 5 Projects + 4 Tell Remi, so the cap cuts the 5th Tell Remi and both Create items.

Keys: ArrowUp and ArrowDown clamp (no wrap). Typing resets i to 0.

engineAlgorithms.name: Note auto-tagging, mentions, recent notes, day list
engineAlgorithms.spec:
tagsFor(text): l = lower-cased text.

Projects, in project order:
- keys = [name, short, ...aliases], lower-cased.
- If ANY non-empty key is a substring of l, add a tag {id, name: short, accent, soft, open: openProject}.

Routines, in routine order:
- keys = [name, short, ...aliases], filtered to length > 3. This drops 'bd8'.
- If a key matches AND NOT (the routine's linked project already matched AND the routine is not flagged co-tag, i.e. not r-ret), add a tag {id, name: (short || name) + ' · BAU', accent: pc-accent (should be the routine's domain), open: openRoutine}.

Projects come first, then routines. Matching is plain substring with no word boundaries, so false positives occur (e.g. 'alpha' in 'alphabet'). Consider word boundaries.

Worked examples:
- n2 → [Returns pipeline, Returns · BAU].
- n3 → [ManCo automation].

Mentions for a day:
- For each saved note, for each tag, count the notes.
- Sort by count descending (stable). Label 'N note(s)'.

recentN:
- Σ notes on the last 5 business days <= TODAY. This is the same set the AI receives as recent_notes, each formatted '{F.s} {HH:MM}: {text}'.

Day list:
- Business days from TODAY back to TODAY - 27, plus any day in that window with notes, plus older days with notes. Descending.
- Week header 'This week' / 'Week of D Mon'.
- Preview = the latest-added note.

totalLine: '{N} notes across {M} days'.

Week spark:
- Mon–Fri of today's week, as calendar days.
- Height = c/max(3, max) %, with a 2px minimum.

dayText (CTA prefill): notes in insertion order, 'HH:MM text' joined with newlines. Production should prefix the date when the day is not today.

engineAlgorithms.name: AI parse validation and simple fallback
engineAlgorithms.spec:
validate(raw):
- open = map from Now-task id to project id, for undone tasks only.
- For each change c:
  - Drop it if !c or !c.type.
  - bau_done: keep only if the routine exists AND occurs today.
  - Every other type needs pmap[project_id].
  - task_done: keep only if open[task_id] === project_id.
  - task_add / scope_add: need text. text = String(text).slice(0,120). hours = clamp(+hours || (task_add ? 1 : 0), 0.25, 80).
  - blocker / note: need text. text sliced to 160.
  - confidence: v = round(+value). Keep if 1 <= v <= 5 and v differs from the current value.
  - target_move: must match /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/ and fall inside the calendar. date = iso(nextBD(dn(date))).
  - hours_per_day: keep if 0 < v <= 8 (capacity).
  - Unknown types are dropped.
- Remove exact duplicates (by JSON.stringify).
- summary = String(raw.summary || ''). unplaced = raw.unplaced filtered, stringified, max 4. Guard against unplaced not being an array.

simple(text), the offline heuristic:
- Keyword map ret / manco / play / fion / alpha. Generalise it to aliases for all projects.
- Split sentences on /(?<=[.!?])\s+|\n+/. last = the focus project.
- For each sentence, lower-cased as l:
  - pid = the first project whose alias or short name appears in l.
  - If l matches /returns (bau|run)|returns are done|returns done/, add bau_done for r-ret and move to the next sentence.
  - pid = pid || last. If still none, push the sentence to unplaced. Otherwise last = pid.
  - h = /(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*(?:h|hr|hrs|hour|hours)\b/. If h matches AND /(want|also|add|scope|new|extra|asked)/ matches, add scope_add. Its text has the hours phrase and any lead-in ('... wants/asked for/add/added ') stripped, a trailing '.' removed, max 80 characters.
  - Blocker: /(?:waiting|blocked|stuck)(?:\s+(?:on|for|by))?\s+([^.;,]+)/.
  - Confidence: /confidence\s*(?:is|at|now|:|of)?\s*(?:a\s+)?([1-5])/.
  - Hours per day: /(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*h(?:ours?)?\s*(?:a|per)\s*day/.
  - If /(finished|done|completed|sent|wrapped|shipped)/ matches, then for each open Now task: take its words longer than 3 letters. Add task_done if hits >= 2, or if (1 <= word count <= 3 and hits >= 1).
  - If no blocker, confidence, scope or rate matched, add a note with the sentence sliced to 140.
- summary = 'Here is what a simple reading picked out. Untick anything that is wrong.' when there are changes.
- The output then goes through validate().

engineAlgorithms.name: Capacity bar segment builder
engineAlgorithms.inputs: DayLoad, capacity, gap, hover id, arrived
engineAlgorithms.spec:
cap = max(total, CAPACITY).

Segment order: BAU items, then project items (in item order), then a free segment when free > 0.

Width = on ? calc(h/cap×100% - gap px) : 0%. Gap is 2px on big bars and 1px on mini bars.

BAU segment:
- Transparent, holding ceil(h) child cells (flex 1, radius 1.5px, 2px or 1px gap).
- Cells are the domain accent, or --overload when the day is over.

Project segment:
- Background: over ? color-mix(overload 20%, paper) : domain soft. The strip variant uses 22%.
- Inset 1px line: overload or accent.

Free segment: transparent with an inset hairline.

Capacity marker: at CAPACITY/cap %, 1px ink, extending 5px above and below the bar. Visible only when over.

Opacity: 0.25 when another id is hovered.

Vertical strip variant (Timeline): segment height = h×5px. BAU uses repeating-linear-gradient(to top, C 0 4px, transparent 4px 5px).

engineAlgorithms.name: Roll tokenizer (odometer)
engineAlgorithms.spec:
Lookup tables:
- DIG = ['', '0'..'9']. WD = Mon..Sun. MON = Jan..Dec.
- col(cells, cur) = {cells, cur, y: 'translateY(' + (-max(0, cells.indexOf(cur))×1.25) + 'em)'}.
- stat(s) = a single fixed cell.

Date form, /^(?:(Mon|…|Sun) )?(\d{1,2}) (Jan|…|Dec)$/:
- [WD col, ' '] if a weekday is present, then tens digit (blank for single-digit days), units digit, ' ', month.

Number form, /^([+−-]?)(\d{1,3})(?:\.(\d))?(\D*)$/:
- sign col ['', '+', '−'] (hyphen-minus becomes U+2212);
- 3 digit cols from padStart(3, ' ') with blanks as '';
- '.' col; decimal digit col; static suffix (e.g. ' BD').

Anything else renders as static text.

Render:
- A hidden full-string sizer, plus an aria-hidden overlay.
- One 1.25em-tall overflow:hidden window per column, sized by its own hidden 'cur'.
- Each window holds a reel of 1.25em cells moved with transform over 440ms spring-soft.
- Columns MUST keep stable keys by position, or the roll won't animate.
- There is no wrap (9 → 0 rolls back down) and column width snaps.
- Add a screen-reader label with the real value.

engineAlgorithms.name: Textbook algorithms
engineAlgorithms.spec:
Heading numbers:
- Walk the blocks in order. h1: c1++, c2 = c3 = 0 → '1'. h2: c2++, c3 = 0 → '1.1'. h3: c3++ → '1.1.1'.
- An h2 before any h1 gives '0.1'.

Word count: Σ over blocks whose type is one of p/h1/h2/h3/bullet/callout of text.trim().split(/\s+/).length.

Tree:
- Top-level pages = pages in the section with no parent, or whose parent is missing (orphans are promoted).
- Depth-first walk in array order. Indent = 4 + depth×16px.

Delete cascade:
- Remove the page and all its descendants.
- Strip page-link blocks that point at removed pages.
- If no pages remain, reseed 'How the Textbook works'.
- Navigate to the surviving parent, or else the first page.

Drop index: the first row whose vertical midpoint is below the cursor, or else the last row.

Block move: splice out, then insert at (idx > from ? idx - 1 : idx).

Section reorder: always inserts before the target.

Chart:
- Height = clamp(200, 900, round(h0 + dy/scale)).
- Accepted files match /\.html?$/i or have type text/html.
- Files over 4 MB get a warning.

Search: case-insensitive substring over titles and block text.

Relative date: floor elapsed days. 0 → 'today', 1 → 'yesterday', otherwise en-GB 'D MMM'.

Recent: the 6 pages with the latest updatedAt. Path = section / ancestor titles. Snippet = first non-empty p or callout.

motionSystem:
Principles, from Foundations:
- 'Alive, never busy. Motion explains a change; nothing loops.'
- Nothing runs longer than 600ms.
- Use ease-out for opacity and colour. These fades are kept under reduced motion.
- Use the spring for layout and movement. It becomes instant under reduced motion.

Tokens:
- --dur-fast 140ms: feedback, hover, press, tick fill, linked highlight.
- --dur-base 240ms: fades, cross-fades, segmented pills.
- --dur-slow 440ms: glides, zoom, drawers.
- --ease-out: cubic-bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1).
- --spring-soft: a critically damped linear() curve with no overshoot, always run at 440ms. It is roughly Motion {type:'spring', bounce:0, visualDuration:0.35}, i.e. stiffness 180, damping 27.
- Implement mostly as CSS transitions keyed off state. The prototype relies on stable DOM nodes, so inline style changes animate from the old computed value. Keep keys stable, especially Roll columns and chart elements.

Reduced motion:
- One source of truth: the OS prefers-reduced-motion setting OR a user setting. This sets :root[data-motion='reduced'].
- --spring-soft becomes steps(1, jump-start), so spatial transitions jump.
- Remove JS-driven translates: arrival offsets, day or month switch slides, and the hover lift.
- Remove the overload pulses, the checkbox scale pop and the moved-chip scale.
- View transitions get 0s duration.
- Smooth scroll becomes auto.
- Opacity and colour fades remain.
- The prototype is inconsistent here (model.reduced only reads the tweak prop); fix that.

1. Screen switching
- All screens stay mounted, so local state and scroll position survive a switch.
- Entering screen: opacity 0→1 over 240ms ease-out after a 60ms delay; visibility flips immediately.
- Leaving screen: opacity 1→0 over 140ms ease-out; visibility becomes hidden at 140ms.
- If production unmounts screens on route change, it must restore scroll and state and emulate this cross-fade.

2. Card to workspace shared-element transition (View Transitions API)
- Sequence:
  1. Set vtPhase='from' on the clicked card; its goal gets view-transition-name 'remi-goal'.
  2. Call document.startViewTransition(() => a promise that resolves after the DOM commits screen=workspace, vtPhase='to', instant=true). The workspace goal textarea is now named 'remi-goal', and the section cross-fade is disabled.
  3. When finished, clear the vt state and set instant=false.
- CSS:
  - ::view-transition-group(remi-goal): 420ms, cubic-bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1).
  - old and new remi-goal: height 100%, width auto, object-fit none, object-position left top (the text grows from top-left without stretching).
  - root: 220ms.
- Skip it when reduced, when startViewTransition is unsupported, when not triggered from a card, or when already on the workspace.
- The goal grows from 26px in the list to 44px.

3. Arrival (first mount only, after a double requestAnimationFrame)
- Today: 5 blocks, opacity 0→1 and translateY(6px)→none over 140ms ease-out, delays 0/40/80/120/160ms. The capacity bar grows from 0 (440ms spring, 90ms delay). Week mini bars grow with a 160ms delay. Month bars grow with an i×8ms stagger.
- Projects: header fades and slides (140ms). Group headers fade (20ms, 120ms). Rows slide 6px with delays of 40 + i×30ms.
- Timeline:
  - bars grow from width 0 (440ms spring, row delay i×30+60ms);
  - rotation segments start at 200 + i×20ms;
  - capacity columns stagger round(i×2.5)ms;
  - diamonds scale 0→1 (240ms ease-out);
  - after 900ms, all delays become 0.
- Home:
  - header 200ms;
  - greeting 180ms opacity + 260ms spring;
  - H1 at +40ms;
  - cards 220ms opacity at +120 and +170ms, 360ms spring;
  - capacity bars i×12ms;
  - Gantt rows i×50+80ms;
  - footer at +240ms.
- Foundations spec: '140 ease-out per block · 40 stagger · 340 total, first load only.'
- Decide whether arrival replays on the first view of a screen. In the prototype it plays hidden at app load.

4. 'The plan moves' (signature, after a check-in)
- The drawer closes immediately. Changes apply 220ms later so the eye is back on the plan. Only the affected bars move.
- Glide: forecast bar width, overrun, end diamond and moved chip 'left' animate over 440ms spring.
- Ghost:
  - the previous-plan dashed bar goes to opacity 1 while flash is set (1100ms), then rests at 0.55 for as long as prev exists;

- Roll: date digits, weekday and month roll over 440ms spring.
- Delta chip: '+N BD' fades in (180ms) and scales 0.9→1 (180ms ease-out, origin left). It holds for 5200ms (moved), then fades. The label is cached so the text survives the fade.
- The Workspace 'moved +N BD' badge follows the same rules. The forecast late tint animates its background over 440ms ease-out.
- A new check-in on the same project restarts the timers.

5. Linked highlight

6. Overlays

- Palette: scrim 140ms; panel opacity 140ms plus translateY(-8px)→0 over 240ms spring; input focused at +30ms.
- Side panels (Timeline 460px, Calendar 440px): translateX(104%)↔0 over 440ms spring plus opacity 240ms. Keep content mounted during exit.
- Date picker: instant. Tooltip: opacity 140ms, position follows the cursor with no transition.

7. Local transitions
- Today day switch: left column fades to 0 (120ms ease-out) and translateX(dir×-8px) over 240ms spring. Swap at 120ms, then return.
- Notes day switch: opacity 140ms and translateY(dir×6px) over 240ms spring. Swap at 120ms; focus the composer at +40ms.
- Calendar month change: opacity 140ms and translateX(dir×-10px) over 240ms spring. Swap at 130ms. Panel prev/next steps change instantly.
- Timeline zoom and pan: every x and width transitions over 440ms spring. Month labels cross-fade 240ms when narrower than 70px. The zoom pill slides over 240ms spring. Pan controls fade 240ms.
- Workspace scrubber:

  - the handle has no transition while dragging and springs 440ms on release;
  - milestones cross-fade by snapshot membership;
  - the body dims to 0.35 over 240ms;
  - hover labels fade over 140ms.
- Capacity segments: width 440ms spring; opacity 140ms.
- Overload pulse: remi-pulse 600ms ease-out, one iteration. Delays: Today bar 300ms, week bar 400ms, Timeline 450ms, Calendar cell 300ms, Calendar panel 200ms. Foundations says 450ms. It does not replay when switching between two overloaded days (same animation string); a keyed restart could fix this.

8. Controls and small feedback
- Checkbox tick: background and border 140ms; glyph opacity 140ms; scale 0.4→1 over 180ms cubic-bezier(0.34,1.5,0.64,1); label colour 240ms; strike-through instant. Foundations and remi-tick disagree (0.6→1.08→1); reconcile.
- Confidence pips: background 240ms.
- Progress fills: width 440ms spring.
- Routines stage dots: 240ms.
- Fresh row flash: accent 8% held 1200/1600ms, background fades over 440ms. Notes version: 7% held 1400ms, fades over 900ms.
- Transition flags: left 440ms spring. Ticks: background 240ms.
- Buttons: nav colours 140ms; primary active scale(0.98), instant; hover instant unless stated.

9. Check-in drawer internals
- Thinking bar: 0→88% over 2600ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0.7,0.3,1).
- Echo lines: opacity and translateY(4px) over 240ms, staggered i×180ms.
- Review groups: opacity 220ms plus translateY(6px) over 320ms spring, staggered k×70ms.
- Row toggle: opacity 1↔0.55 over 140ms.

10. Home
- Card hover: lift -4px (360ms spring), box-shadow border 240ms, arrow nudge 2px spring.
- CAP to CAPH bars re-stagger. Overrun width animates.
- Typewriter: max-width 0→9ch, steps(9) over 520ms.
- Slash menu: opacity 200ms plus translateY(-4px) over 320ms spring, delayed 560ms on enter and 0ms on exit.
- Expand overlay:
  - place the overlay over the card at radius 6, then fade it in over 140ms;
  - at +120ms animate left, top, width, height and radius to the full stage over 420ms spring;
  - navigate at +520ms.
- Going home from the app or Textbook: fade opacity over 180ms ease-out, then navigate.

11. Textbook
- Sidebar: grid columns 288↔56 over 440ms spring; panel translateX(-24px) with opacity.
- Chevrons: rotate over 240ms spring.
- Page swap: fade 140ms plus translateY(6px) over 240ms spring, swap at 120ms.
- Home cards: stagger i×50ms.
- New block: held at opacity 0 and translateY(4px) for 60ms, then animated in (220ms opacity, 320ms spring).
- Iframe height: 440ms spring.
- Toast: opacity 240ms plus translateY(8px) over 440ms spring.
- Drop overlay: 140ms.
aiIntegration:
CURRENT FLOW (CheckIn.dc.html)

1. The user opens Tell Remi. Entry points:
   - the header button (focus = workspace project, else none);
   - palette 'Tell Remi about X';
   - palette quick-add '+6h returns', which prefills 'New scope on <short>, about 6h: ';
   - the Timeline panel, the Workspace, and the Projects 'Check in now' button;
   - Notes 'Turn this day into an update', which prefills 'HH:MM text' lines.
2. The user types free text and presses Send or ⌘↵.
3. The client calls:
   window.claude.complete({system: SYS, max_tokens: 1800, messages: [{role: 'user', content: 'CONTEXT\n' + JSON.stringify(context) + '\n\nUPDATE\n' + text}]})
   No model id, temperature or streaming is set.

The CONTEXT payload:
- today: 'YYYY-MM-DD (Monday 5 October, BD3)'
- focus_project: project id or null
- projects[], each with: {id, name, short, domain (display name), forecast, target, hours_per_day, confidence, open_tasks: [{id, text, hours}] (undone Now tasks only), milestones: ['name (date)']}
- routines[], each with: {id, name, rule text, runs_today}
- recent_notes: every note from the last 5 business days up to today, formatted 'Fri 2 Oct 16:10: text'

The system prompt (verbatim in CheckIn.dc.html lines 127–145):
- It asks for a single JSON object {summary, changes[], unplaced[]}.
- It defines nine change types with examples: task_done, task_add, scope_add ('a day' = 8h), blocker, confidence (1–5, only if stated), target_move (YYYY-MM-DD), hours_per_day, note (20 words max), bau_done (a routine that runs today).
- It says recent_notes are background only.
- Rules: be conservative and never invent work; match by name, short name or obvious reference; focus_project captures remarks that name no other project; resolve relative dates against today; at most one note per project; prefer task_done over note.

4. Reply handling:
   - Take the greedy match /\{[\s\S]*\}/ and JSON.parse it.
   - Run validate(). Its rules (id existence, open-task ownership, clamps and length limits, confidence must differ from the current value, target snapped to the next business day and inside the calendar, 0 < hours_per_day <= 8, bau_done only if the routine runs today, dedupe) are in engineAlgorithms.
   - If window.claude is absent, the 'simple reading' regex parser runs instead.
   - Any other error shows an error panel with 'Try again' and 'Use a simple reading'.
5. Review: changes are grouped per project, each shown with a live forecast EffectChip. The user unticks anything wrong.
6. Apply: saveCheckIn closes the drawer and applies the accepted changes 220ms later (applyUpdate, then applyCheckIn).

PRODUCTION DESIGN

- Move the AI call server-side: POST /api/checkins/parse. The browser never holds credentials. SPEC: 'the server can later … hold AI credentials'.
- core/config holds:
  - aiProvider: 'none' | 'anthropic' | 'firm-gateway' (e.g. Claude through a firm-approved cloud tenancy) | 'local' (an on-device model);
  - model id, timeout and max tokens (1800);
  - aiSendRecentNotes (boolean);
  - redaction options.
- The context is built server-side from the DB, not trusted from the client.
- Use structured output: tool use with a JSON schema for the Change union, instead of the greedy regex. Validate with the shared zod schema and then the validate() business rules, and return {summary, changes, unplaced, source}.
- Keep the deterministic 'simple reading' fallback, and make it the default when AI is off. Generalise it: keywords come from the EntityAlias table plus project and routine names and short names, not the hard-coded ret/manco/play/fion/alpha/r-ret lists. Unify it with the Notes tagger.
- Fix the fallback quirks:
  - blocker text is lower-cased;
  - a note is added alongside task_done;
  - both scope_add and hours_per_day come from the same sentence.
- Support cancellation (AbortController) and a session guard, so a late reply cannot land in a newly opened drawer.
- Keep the review-before-apply contract: AI output is only ever a proposal. Store the accepted changes with rawText and source on the CheckIn record and in the event log.
- Apply runs in one server transaction and returns movements for the animation.
- Decide on the structured form: SPEC §7.4 and the brief wanted a structured form with live preview (screenshot 02-sig), plus the free-text box as the future state. The code ships only the free-text flow. If the structured form is rebuilt, it uses POST /api/projects/:id/checkins and preview-shift.

'STAY LOCAL' IMPLICATIONS (SPEC: 'Nothing leaves the Mac'; open question 6)

- Each AI parse sends the following off the machine:
  - the free text;
  - every project's name, short name, dates, hours per day and confidence;
  - open task text and hours;
  - milestone names and dates;
  - routine names and rules;
  - full text of the last 5 business days of notes.
  It does NOT send goals, charters or risks.
- This needs compliance sign-off on which route is permitted: a firm-approved Claude route, a local model, or none.
- Until sign-off, ship with aiProvider = 'none' (simple reading only). Show a clear indicator of which provider is in use. Consider an audit log of exactly what was sent, and a toggle to exclude notes.
- The Notes rail copy 'Notes from your last five business days go along with every Tell Remi update' must reflect the real setting.

OTHER NETWORK EGRESS TO REMOVE FOR STAY-LOCAL

- Google Fonts and Material Symbols: self-host.
- React, ReactDOM and Babel from unpkg: bundle them.
- KaTeX from jsDelivr: bundle it.
- Textbook live-chart iframes run arbitrary user HTML with scripts and network access (the sample chart fetches Google Fonts). Serve chart content with a restrictive CSP (connect-src 'none', font and style limited to self), or from an isolated local origin, and keep sandbox='allow-scripts' without allow-same-origin.
- Future integrations (Outlook meetings reducing capacity, Excel import) belong in the server and likely need IT sign-off.
persistenceToday:
Everything lives in browser localStorage. There is no backend.

1) 'remi.v1', written by Remi.dc.html (the app shell)

The whole-state JSON blob:
- projects: Project[] in stored shape (not derived);
- tasks: {taskId: boolean};
- doneOn: {taskId: ISO};
- feed: FeedEvent[], where 'when' is a display string such as 'Just now' or 'Sat 3 Oct' and ids are 'f' + Date.now();
- funds: boolean[12], today's returns-run ticks, not keyed by date;
- routines: Routine[];
- bauDone: {'<routineId>:<ISO occurrence>': ISO done date};
- notes: {ISO day: [{id: 'n' + base36, t: 'HH:MM', text}]};
- m2: true.

Loading:
- The blob is read once at module evaluation.
- It is accepted only if projects is an array. Otherwise each slice falls back to its seed: BASE_PROJECTS, ROUTINES, BASE_FEED, funds with the first 5 ticked, tasks {ret-1, fi-1}, BASE_NOTES, and BASE_DONE_ON {ret-1: 2026-10-01, fi-1: 2026-10-02}.
- normalize() and normR() fill in defaults.
- Migration m2 inserts task man-0 ('Send the NAV bridge spec to Finance', 0.5h, due 2026-10-02) at the start of manco now[0] when it is missing.

Saving:
- In componentDidUpdate, a 250ms debounce fires when any of the 8 slices changes by reference.
- Errors (quota, private mode) are swallowed.
- The very first state change after mount is skipped.

Resetting:
- 'Reset to sample data' in the palette removes the key and restores the seeds.

Not persisted: screen, ws, hover, drawer, palette, flash/moved, the view-transition state and requests. A reload always opens Today with ws = 'ret'.

2) 'remi.textbook.v1', written by Remi Textbook.dc.html

Shape: {cur, pages: [{id, section, parent?, title, updated, blocks: [...]}], sections: [{id, label, accent}], secCollapsed}.
- Chart HTML is stored inline as strings.
- The seed chart uses the src marker 'charts/price-yield.html', hydrated from the SAMPLE_CHART constant.
- Saved with a 350ms debounce on every mutation, including navigation and each resize pointermove.
- On a quota error it shows a toast.
- cur is forced to '__home' on load.

3) Remi Home.dc.html is read-only. It reads both keys for its counts, using the hard-coded key notes['2026-10-05'].

4) Foundations has no persistence.

ID generation relies on Date.now() and base36, so collisions are possible.
